note: Adapted from the original description by Holmgren (1911), in German; the alate and the soldier are given, the worker description in the original not being used. Part of the measurement table is damaged by OCR and only the legible values are entered.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Black to blackish brown; anteclypeus, labrum, antennae, the T-shaped mark on the pronotum and on the meso- and metanotum, femora, tarsi and the middle of the abdominal sternites paler; wings black. Hairs on the head, pronotum and abdomen rather dense. Head oval; compound eyes small; ocelli small, their distance from the compound eyes hardly exceeding their diameter; fontanelle indistinct; postclypeus as convex as the frons, strongly convex behind, its anterior margin straight, reaching the mandibular articulation; anteclypeus rather large; labrum wider than long; antennae 11-segmented, segment 3 very small and ring-like, segment 4 distinctly shorter than segment 2, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum small, trapezoidal, the anterior margin slightly concave; posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum broadly truncate; fore wing scale slightly larger than the hind wing scale. Wing membrane densely covered with fine dots and sparsely with fine hairs; media very close to the cubitus, with 1—3 branches; cubitus with 7—9 branches, the basal ones often very oblique. Cerci short; styles short, present in the male. Measurements: body length including the wings 8—9, body length without wings 5, head length 1.02, head width 0.87, pronotum width 0.64 mm. Queen with an uneven surface bearing warts and sparse hairs, body length 16, width 4 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow, slightly brownish in front; mandibles brown except at the base; body nearly white to yellowish white. Hairs not especially dense, but not truly sparse either. Head rectangular and rather thick, obliquely truncate (bluntly rounded) in front; fontanelle rather indistinct; head sutures very indistinct; anterior margin of the postclypeus straight, its posterior boundary very indistinctly angular; labrum oval and blunt; mandibles relatively short and wide, slightly curved, the inner margin very finely and irregularly toothed; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 much smaller and narrower than segment 2, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2 and very indistinctly thicker, segment 6 slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped, the anterior margin distinctly concave, the posterior margin not concave. Cerci short, with styles.
